newsitem.title: ITALY: ATHLETICS-FREDERICKS SUGGESTS ROME DROP OLYMPIC BID.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-FREDERICKS SUGGESTS ROME DROP OLYMPIC BID.

text.p: Namibian Frankie Fredericks on Wednesday performed an act of sporting bravery equivalent to entering the lion's den in search of a new convert to vegetarianism.

The sprinter told a news conference in Rome, before local reporters and in a room full of publicity for the Italian capital's bid for the 2004 Summer Olympics, that the city should consider standing down in favour of Cape Town.
"It would be very nice if Rome pulled out of the race," said Fredericks, in Rome for an international athletics meeting on Thursday. "I mean, they already had the Olympics once.
"I think that if South Africa does not get it this time, then I don't know if any African country will ever get it in the future," said the 1996 Olympic 100 and 200 metres silver medallist.
"I think Cape Town would make a very nice Olympics. Maybe Rome will pull out and all the others too and then South Africa will be the only ones left."
Rome, who hosted the 1960 Games, are considered one of the frontrunners for the 2004 Olympics.
